chapter_theme: Last songs at Thiruchengode (திருச்செங்கோடு, 2 of 2), the serpent hill: the poet asks not to fall with his impure body into hell, to be freed from the tangle of wealth-lust and women, and from the illusion that a bubble-like life with wife, sons and house will last for aeons; he gives thanks for the grace that set him to sing the Thiruppugazh, and asks Murugan to come on the peacock to the battle in which his servant defeats Death.
structure_note: Six songs. 600 and 604 are in dense, clipped rhythms whose word divisions are often unsure. 602 is a thanksgiving for the book, 603 a meditation on impermanence, 605 a death-hour plea that names Arunai although it stands under Thiruchengode. The shrine is named as சர்ப்பகிரி, பணிசயிலம், the serpent hill.

600.reading: The poet asks whether he, a servant, should drive this impure body about and fall into the fiery hell; the opening lines, which seem to describe a mountain, a great tree heavy with flowers and fruit and a place he should not speak of, are too broken by the rhythm for a sure reading. The praise names the leaping deer and the sage of the Upanishads (Valli's birth), Murugan's twelve shoulders that embraced the hunters' parrot-like girl sweet as honey and nectar, and the emerald and gold peacock that carried him against the demon clans.
600.nuance: மலவுடல் நடத்தி எரிகொள் நிரயத்தின் இடை அடிமை விழலாமோ is the one clear plea: the body is called impure (மல) and the fear is of hell, not of rebirth. The praise's தத்து கவன வரிணத்து உபநிட விதத்து முநி seems to allude to Valli's birth from a deer to a sage. The first eight lines run syllables together (அத்து கிரினலது ரத்து அலனவள கத்து ...) and I cannot divide them with confidence.

601.reading: The poet confesses that, gripped by desire for wealth and looking on, he became kin to parrot-like women and was distracted in a loveless company, his mind running to clasp their shoulders; he asks whether he will call his mind back, cut the tangle of a false life, gain firm and beautiful speech, praise Murugan and adorn him with vetchi flowers. The praise names Murugan king over kings, holder of the cock and the vel at the serpent hill, and the true word of the right path of reasoning that establishes the tattvas, forty-eight and forty-eight.
601.nuance: அத்த வேட்கை, desire for wealth (அத்தம்), stands first, before the women. தத்வ நாற்பத்தெட்டு நாற்பத்தெட்டு makes ninety-six, the larger Saiva count of the tattvas; Murugan is the true teaching (சத்ய வாக்யம்) of the logic-shastra that sets them out. கொத்து நூற்றுப் பத்து நாட்ட is unclear to me.

602.reading: The poet says he will never forget the grace by which Murugan appeared to him and set even him, a small servant, to sing the Thiruppugazh, rich in the sound of beautiful poetry, which devotees in the east, west, south and north recite as a wonder, so that it spread through the world. The praise names the hunter girl who guarded the millet slinging stones at the screaming parrots and whom Murugan embraced, and Murugan as the one who taught the whole of the Vedas' truth and the Supreme to his father, who keeps Shakti on his left side, at the serpent hill.
602.nuance: This is the book naming itself again: திருப்புகழைச் சிறிது அடியேனும் செப்பென வைத்து, the grace of being set to sing it, and தெரிசித்த, that Murugan showed himself. Here it is already sung in the four directions. மறைநூலின் தத்துவ தற்பரம் முற்றும் உணர்த்திய is the teaching of Siva without naming Om.

603.reading: The poet says that he lives in the illusion that this life, impermanent as a bubble, in a false hut of a body, with wife, sons, house and friends, is an unshaken greatness that will stand for a crore of aeons, and asks Murugan to think of a way for the love he has set daily on his feet to stay. The praise names Murugan lord of the serpent hill, delight of the three Tamils, nephew of the one with discus and mace, the Brahmin of Kazhi who impaled the dumb arguing Jains, and lord of the hunters' daughter whose chastity never failed.
603.nuance: புற்புதம், the bubble, and ஒரு கோடி கற்பம், a crore of aeons, set the real span of life against the imagined one; நிட்டை, a steady state, is used ironically of the illusion. தர்க்க சமண் மூகர் மிக்க கழு ஏற வைத்த ஒரு காழி மறையோன் is Sambandar's story told of Murugan.

604.reading: In a clipped, hammering rhythm the poet describes women whose breasts are bound in green silk bodices worked with gold and likened to lotus buds, praised by young men, and asks not to wander in their stony-hearted, false madness, loving them and being struck; he asks Murugan to teach him with love the word by which he may learn and attain, and to give his victorious anklets. The praise hears the cock crow (குக்குக்குக்), names Murugan the bearer of the cock banner and the life of Kochai, and ends at the high serpent hill.
604.nuance: பொய்ப் பித்தம், false madness, is the poet's word for the infatuation. கொச்சைப் பதி is a name of Sirkazhi, Sambandar's town, so the praise may again make Murugan Sambandar. The song is built almost entirely of doubled consonants (கற்சித்தச் சுத்தப் பொய்ப்பித்தத்திற் புக்கு), and many divisions, especially in the closing lines on Daksha (தக்ஷப் பற்றுக்கு), are guesses.

605.reading: The poet asks that, on the day when cruel Death and his army fall as Murugan's stammering servant, who worships his two feet, fights with his grace, Murugan come once to Arunai to see that battle, mounted on the emerald horse with his six faces, many eyes, his shoulders that embraced the hunter girl and his sun-bright banner, while old devotees and the gods praise him on both sides with Tamil and the Vedas. The praise lists Siva's emblems, matted hair, poison, serpents, axe, moon, fire, drum, deer, and the many-mouthed river, names Murugan his son, and ends with the battle against the night-roaming demons.
605.nuance: The plea reverses the usual fear: the servant himself fights Death (கொடிய மறலியும் அவனது கடகமும் மடிய) with the Lord's grace, and asks Murugan only to come and watch (அமர் காண). அருணையில் ஒருவிசை வரவேணும் names Thiruvannamalai inside a Thiruchengode song; பணி சயில, the serpent hill, is the local name in the praise.

links.note: Both thank Murugan for the grace of being told to sing the Thiruppugazh (செப்பென); 2 lists what the song must hold, and 602 already hears it recited by devotees in all four directions.

The Kural calls it the lowest folly to take what does not last for what lasts; 603 confesses exactly that folly, living as if a bubble-like life with wife, sons and house would stand for a crore of aeons.
Both see life as a bubble (புற்புதம்). The Naladiyar praises those who see it so and resolve to end their wandering; 603 confesses that he knows the image and still lives as if it lasted.
8 asks Murugan to come on the peacock when Death's men strike and end his fear; 605 turns the same hour into a battle the servant wins with Murugan's grace, and asks him to come and watch.

The praise calls Murugan the true word of the right path of reasoning that establishes the tattvas, forty-eight and forty-eight (தத்வ நாற்பத்தெட்டு நாற்பத்தெட்டு மேற்றுத் ... சத்ய வாக்யப் பெருமாளே), that is ninety-six. Tirumular says the ninety-six are called common to all, while the thirty-six are the tattvas of the Saivas (தொண்ணூறோடு ஆறும் பொதுஎன்பர் ... ஆறாறு அருஞ்சைவர் தத்துவம்). The Tirumanthiram places the song's count as the shared reckoning of all schools, beside a narrower Saiva count of thirty-six.

The poet says he will never forget the grace that set even him, a small servant, to sing the Thiruppugazh (திருப்புகழைச் சிறிது அடியேனுஞ் செப்பென வைத்து ... அநுக்ரகம் மறவேனே). Tirumular says the Lord made him well so that he would render the Lord well in Tamil (என்னைநன் றாக இறைவன் படைத்தனன் தன்னைநன் றாகத் தமிழ்செய்யு மாறே). Both poets present their own Tamil work as appointed by the god, not chosen.

The song asks Murugan to come and watch the day when his stammering servant, who worships the two feet, fights with his grace and cruel Death and his army fall (கொடிய மறலியு மவனது கடகமு மடிய ... நினதருள் கொடுபொரு மமர்காண). The Kural says that for those who have gained the strength of austerity even leaping past Death becomes possible (கூற்றம் குதித்தலும் கைகூடும்). Both let a human being overcome Death; the Kural grants it to the strength of tapas, the song to the servant fighting with the Lord's grace.

source_issues: Song 605 names Arunai (அருணையில் ஒருவிசை வரவேணும்) though it is grouped under Thiruchengode; the praise's பணி சயில, serpent hill, fits Thiruchengode.
